claims.text: The initial material is an as-deposited CrMnFeCoNi high-entropy-alloy bond coat.
Oxidation of CrMnFeCoNi preferentially produces manganese-rich surface oxides and depletes Mn beneath the scale.
The manganese-rich oxides formed on CrMnFeCoNi are non-protective.
A moderate-temperature pre-oxidation treatment at controlled oxygen partial pressure will preferentially form an Al2O3-rich layer on CrMnFeCoNi.
The pre-oxidation treatment will produce a continuous, thin alumina scale.
A continuous alumina scale will act as a diffusion barrier at the bond-coat surface.
Mn diffuses outward rapidly during oxidation and thereby promotes manganese-rich oxide formation.
The proposed alumina scale will slow oxygen ingress.
The proposed alumina scale will suppress outward Mn diffusion and the formation of irregular, non-protective oxide scales.
Reducing elemental depletion through alumina-scale formation will improve adhesion and reduce spallation during thermal cycling.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will have a more uniform and adherent oxide scale than untreated bond coats.
Pre-oxidized bond coats will oxidize more slowly and undergo less degradation than untreated bond coats.
Untreated CrMnFeCoNi exhibits vigorous Mn-rich oxidation and associated Mn depletion in air.
The intervention should remain protective in oxidizing service environments up to approximately 1100 °C under cyclic thermal stress.
Extreme thermal cycling or very high oxygen pressure may exceed the protective capability of the alumina scale.

contradictions.description: The stated CrMnFeCoNi alloy contains no Al, yet the intervention is asserted to form an Al2O3-rich scale without adding an aluminum source or modifying the alloy composition.

The falsification rule lists 'less Mn depletion' among conditions for falsification, although less Mn depletion is a predicted improvement. This makes the decisive failure condition logically ambiguous.
